newsitem.title: SPAIN: Basque officials blamed for mishandling ETA case.
newsitem.headline: Basque officials blamed for mishandling ETA case.

text.p: Spain's government sacked one senior Basque official on Monday and a second resigned for mishandling the case of an ETA suspect hospitalised in serious condition two days after his arrest.
Interior Minister Jaime Mayor Oreja said an investigation by his ministry into whether prisoner Fernando Elejalde had been tortured in police custody found there was no maltreatment.

But Guipuzcoa province civil governor Angel Goya and San Sebastian police commissioner Emilio Monge were criticised for failing to tell the government that Elejalde was badly wounded upon his arrest and for delaying his medical care.

"Goya presented his resignation and it was accepted. The police commissioner was fired for political responsibility on one side and also for statements he made to the press," an Interior Ministry spokesman said.

Monge, in an interview published on Saturday in the daily El Mundo, said he had given more information to the ministry than he was required to. He added that Interior Ministry officials should stay out of police anti-terrorist activity.

The ministry ordered an investigation into whether Elejalde had been tortured shortly after he was taken to hospital on Thursday semi-conscious and suffering from four crushed vertebrae, a ruptured kidney, a perforated eardrum and bruises.
Police arrested Elejalde on Tuesday after a gun battle on the streets of the Basque city of San Sebastian as he fled the scene of the killing of a prison psychologist.
Officials said the suspect, 29, is a member of the violent separatist group ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom).
"He was not tortured nor was there maltreatment in the San Sebastian police station," Mayor Oreja told a parliamentary committee when he presented the inquiry findings on Monday.

A High Court judge who interviewed Elejalde in a Madrid hospital on Saturday also found no evidence of torture and said the suspect had admitted to Tuesday's killing and to the killing of a bicycle vendor earlier this year.
The judge, in a court order on Monday, formally charged Elejalde with the murder of the psychologist, with belonging to an armed band and illegal possession of weapons.

Elejalde's defence lawyer said at the weekend that he was beaten while in police custody, just after his arrest and on Wednesday and Thursday. He was taken to an emergency clinic two hours after his arrest.

"He told us the blows he received started when he arrived at the police station and that none of the injuries was a result of the arrest," lawyer Ainhoa Baigliot said on Sunday. "They put him on his knees and hit him with an unknown instrument."

But Mayor Oreja said the ministry's inquiry found that the injuries reported on Tuesday "clearly coincided" with those reported two days later, showing that he was hurt during the arrest and not by torture.
The minister said "proportional" force was used in the arrest considering the suspect was armed and dangerous and was fleeing the scene of a killing.
Officials said earlier that Elejalde was not taken to the hospital again until Thursday because he did not tell police he was in pain.
